runs.text: Arr, we hold these truths to be self-evident, shipmate, that all men be created equal, that they be endowed by their Creator with certain unalienable Rights, that among these be Life, Liberty, and the pursuit of Happiness. To secure these rights, Governments be set up among Men, drawin' their just powers from the consent of the governed — that whenever any Form of Government turns rotten against these ends, it be the Right of the crew to alter or scuttle it, and to raise up new Government, layin' its keel on such principles and riggin' its powers in such form, as to them shall seem most likely to steer their Safety and Happiness. Prudence, indeed, will chart the course that Governments long established should not be changed for light and passin' tides; and so all experience hath shown, that mankind be more disposed to weather the storm, while evils be bearable, than to right themselves by scuttlin' the forms they be accustomed to. But when a long train of abuses and usurpations, holdin' steady on the same course, shows a design to drag 'em down under absolute Despotism, it be their right, it be their duty, to cast off such Government, and set new Guards at the helm for their future security.

runs.text:
Arr, listen well, shipmate, for these truths be plain as a clear horizon: all men be created equal on this voyage o' life, and their Creator be the one who granted 'em rights no soul can strip away — Life, Liberty, and the chasin' o' Happiness. To keep these rights safe, crews o' Governments be set upon the deck o' Men, and they draw their rightful power only from the consent o' them they govern. And whenever any Form o' Government turns rotten and works against these ends, 'tis the right o' the People to alter her course or scuttle her entire, and lay down a new vessel o' Government, settin' her keel on such principles and riggin' her powers in such form as seems most likely to bring 'em safe to Happiness's port.

Prudence, mind ye, would have it that Governments long held to their moorings ought not be cast off for light and passin' squalls; and sure as the tide, all experience hath shown that mankind be more willin' to suffer, while the troubles can be borne, than to right their own ship by scrappin' the forms they've grown used to sailin' under. But when a long chain o' abuses and thievin' o' power, all pointin' toward one and the same design, shows plain that they mean to drag the crew down into absolute Despotism, then it be their right, aye, their very duty, to throw such Government overboard and set new watchmen at the helm for their future security.
